Purpose Physique athletes engage in rigorous competition preparation involving intense energy restriction and physical training to enhance muscle definition. This study investigates hormonal changes and their physiological and performance impacts during such preparation. Methods Participants included female (10 competing (COMP) and 10 non-dieting controls (CTRL)) and male (13 COMP and 10 CTRL) physique athletes. COMP participants were tested 23 weeks before (PRE), one week before (MID), and 23 weeks after the competition (POST). Non-dieting CTRL participants were tested at similar intervals. Measurements included body composition (DXA), muscle cross-sectional area (ultrasound), energy availability (EA) derived by subtracting exercise energy expenditure (EEE) from energy intake (EI) and dividing by fat-free mass (FFM), muscle strength, and various serum hormone concentrations (ACTH, cortisol, estradiol, FSH, IGF-1, IGFBP-3, insulin, and free and total testosterone and SHBG). Results During the diet, EA ( p < 0.001), IGF-1 ( p < 0.001), IGFBP-3 ( p < 0.01), and absolute muscle strength ( p < 0.01–0.001) decreased significantly in both sexes in COMP. Decreases in IGF-1 were also associated with higher loss in FFM. In males, testosterone ( p < 0.01) and free testosterone ( p < 0.05) decreased, while SHBG ( p < 0.001) and cortisol ( p < 0.05) increased. Insulin decreased significantly only in males ( p < 0.001). Mood disturbances, particularly increased fatigue in males ( p < 0.05), highlighted the psychological strain of competition preparation. All these changes were restored by increased EA during the post-competition recovery period. Conclusion Significant reductions in IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 during competition preparation may serve as biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress. This study offers valuable insights into hormonal changes, muscle strength, and mood state during energy-restricted intense training. Keywords Energy availability IGF-1 Weight loss Bodybuilding POMS REDs Finnish Fitness Sports Association Renaissance Periodization University of Jyväskylä (JYU) Open Access funding provided by University of Jyväskylä (JYU). issue-copyright-statement © Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2025 Introduction Physique athletes undergo rigorous competition preparation with intense energy restriction and physical training to enhance muscle definition. This preparatory phase is followed by a recovery period of 3–4 months, during which body composition and endocrine changes are typically restored (Hulmi et al. 2017 ; Rossow et al. 2013 ). The off-season focuses on muscle growth through balanced nutrition and resistance training (Mursu et al. 2023 ). Hormone profiles in elite athletes differ from usual reference ranges, potentially reflecting baseline differences between athletes and the general population as well as the impact of athletic training on the endocrine systems (Healy et al. 2014 ). We previously reported that physique athletes experience significant hormonal changes during the competition preparation. These inevitable changes, likely caused by the combined factors of weight loss, training and dieting stress, and the sustained energy deficit, include reduced leptin and T3 levels and increased ghrelin concentrations, reflecting shifts in energy metabolism (Isola et al. 2023 ). Weight loss also alters serum cardiometabolic profiles, such as insulin, highlighting metabolic complexities (Jouhki et al. 2024 ; Mäestu et al. 2010 ). Additionally, male athletes experience fluctuations in insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), free (FT), and total testosterone (T), while female athletes demonstrate changes in estradiol levels during the preparation (Hulmi et al. 2017 ; Mitchell et al. 2018 ). Athletes may also experience reductions in muscular function, strength, and power as the focus shifts toward achieving ideal body aesthetics sometimes at the expense of exercise performance (Robinson et al. 2015 ). Additionally, bone mineral density (BMD) can decrease during periods of energy deficit, but it often recovers during refeeding (Hulmi et al. 2017 ). The physiological stress from the competition preparation may lead to disruptions in sleep patterns, mood disturbances, and alterations in nutrient intake, which collectively contribute to diminished exercise performance (Longstrom et al. 2020 ). The concept of relative energy deficiency in sport (RED-S) expands our understanding of low energy availability (LEA) impacts. Affecting both male and female athletes, RED-S leads to hormonal imbalances, decreased bone mineral density, and weakened immune function. Energy deficiency also reduces muscle strength, power, and endurance, and can cause mood disturbances, anxiety, and depression. These changes impair reproductive function, metabolism, and overall health, causing conditions like hypothalamic amenorrhea in females and reduced fertility in males. Ultimately, RED-S compromises health, well-being, and athletic performance (Angelidi et al. 2024 ). This study examined serum hormonal changes in physique athletes during the competition preparation. Understanding hormonal alterations vital to training and health outcomes is paramount, as it may inform coaching strategies. This research delves into how energy restriction and intense training impact hormone profiles, physiological performance, and psychological well-being, using the profile of mood states (POMS) to assess mood changes. We hypothesized that the competition diets would lead to changes in serum hormones, BMD, performance, and mood in both sexes. These findings may potentially improve coaching methods for supporting athletes while minimizing adverse effects from competition preparation.

extracted_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in both male and female COMP groups (p < 0.001) during competition preparation (PRE to MID) compared to CTRL. These decreases were associated with higher loss in FFM. Levels did not significantly change from MID to POST in COMP groups, with female COMP showing persistently lower levels compared to CTRL (p < 0.05) after MID.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Crucial hormone for muscle development, growth, cell proliferation, tissue repair, and anabolism, playing a significant role in metabolism and regulated by nutrition.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During intense energy restriction and physical training in physique athletes' competition preparation (PRE to MID) and subsequent recovery (MID to POST), specifically under conditions of reduced energy intake and low energy availability.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a potential biomarker for monitoring physiological stress and an anabolic deficit, reflecting a compromised anabolic state and correlation with loss in fat-free mass under energy restriction. Lower levels suggest a catabolic state or reduced anabolic drive.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in both female and male COMP groups during competition preparation (p < 0.01). There was also a significant difference between sexes at baseline (p < 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: The main binding protein for IGF-1, it regulates IGF-1's transport, half-life, and bioavailability, thereby modulating its anabolic actions.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During intense energy restriction and physical training in physique athletes' competition preparation, under conditions of energy deficits.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a potential biomarker for monitoring physiological stress, as decreased levels may alter IGF-1 bioavailability, contributing to reduced IGF-1 activity and compromised anabolic capacity during energy restriction; aligns with energy deficits and body composition changes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly differed between male and female COMP at baseline (p < 0.001). Decreased significantly in male COMP from PRE to MID (p < 0.01) and compared to CTRL (p < 0.05), with a significant difference in change between sexes (p < 0.05). No significant changes were observed in female COMP groups. Levels in male COMP increased from MID to POST, recovering back to baseline (p < 0.001), also significant compared to CTRL (p < 0.05). Female CTRL showed a decrease from MID to POST (p < 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A key anabolic steroid hormone involved in muscle protein synthesis, growth, bone density, red blood cell production, and male reproductive health. In females, it contributes to bone health, mood, and libido, and is regulated by the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During competition preparation (dieting, energy restriction, intense training) in physique athletes and subsequent recovery phase.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased levels in males suggest a catabolic state, physiological stress, or HPG axis disruptions, potentially impairing muscle anabolism, recovery, and overall male health. Its recovery indicates a return of anabolic hormonal balance. Stability in females suggests different hormonal responses. Overall, it plays a critical role in maintaining muscle mass and optimizing performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly differed between male and female COMP at baseline (p < 0.001). No significant changes were observed in female COMP groups. Levels in male COMP increased from MID to POST, recovering back to baseline (p < 0.05), also significant compared to CTRL (p < 0.001).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: The biologically active, bioavailable form of testosterone that directly interacts with target tissues to exert anabolic and androgenic effects, crucial for muscle maintenance and overall male health. In females, its levels correlate with changes in maximal strength and/or muscle cross-sectional area.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During competition preparation (dieting, energy restriction, intense training) in physique athletes and the subsequent 5-month recovery phase.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased levels in males signify reduced bioavailable testosterone, directly impacting anabolic processes, physical performance, and overall male health under energy restriction and intense training. Indicates hormonal adaptation and HPG axis disruptions. Recovery indicates a return of active anabolic hormonal balance. Stability in females suggests different hormonal responses.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (during preparation), lower (males during recovery), unchanged (females during recovery)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Differed between sexes at baseline in COMP (p < 0.001). Increased in both female (p < 0.05) and male (p < 0.001) COMP from PRE to MID, with male COMP differing significantly from CTRL (p < 0.001). From MID to POST, SHBG levels decreased in male COMP (p < 0.05), while male CTRL increased (p < 0.05). No significant changes were observed in female groups from MID to POST.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A glycoprotein that binds to sex hormones (e.g., testosterone, estradiol) in the blood, regulating their transport and bioavailability; approximately 65% of testosterone is bound to SHBG.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During competition preparation, especially with significant weight loss and reduced caloric intake, and during the subsequent recovery phase.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels, particularly when combined with lower testosterone, indicate reduced availability of free (bioavailable) testosterone, exacerbating catabolic effects and impacting androgen-dependent functions. Monitoring is important for maintaining muscle mass and optimizing performance. Recovery phase decrease suggests a return towards baseline free sex hormone concentrations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly in male COMP during competition preparation (p < 0.05, PRE to MID). Increased significantly in male COMP from MID to POST (p < 0.05), but not significantly different from CTRL. Female athletes showed an upward trend during competition preparation, though not statistically significant. No significant changes were observed in female groups across the study for specific time points.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During competition preparation (dieting, energy restriction, intense training) and the subsequent recovery phase in physique athletes, suggesting an adaptive response to energy stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels in males indicate increased physiological stress, potentially promoting catabolism and impairing recovery. A persistent increase during recovery suggests ongoing physiological stress. Stability or non-significant changes in females may indicate different stress coping mechanisms.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects perceived tiredness, exhaustion, and low energy levels.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Across PRE to MID and MID to POST phases in male and female physique athletes and control groups.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher scores indicate psychological stress, potential overtraining, or reduced recovery capacity during the competition preparation phase. A decrease indicates recovery from psychological stress and fatigue. Stability in females suggests different psychological responses regarding fatigue.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (males PRE to MID), lower (females PRE to MID)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TENSION increased in male COMP from PRE to MID (p < 0.05), though not significantly different from CTRL. Significant sex differences were noted in TENSION changes from PRE to MID (p < 0.01), with female TENSION decreasing. No significant difference was noted within female COMP groups from PRE to MID.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects perceived muscular tension, nervousness, and anxiety.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Across the PRE to MID phase in male and female physique athletes and control groups.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher scores in males indicate psychological stress or anxiety during the activity phase. Lower scores in females suggest reduced psychological stress or improved coping mechanisms. Stability in female COMP suggests consistent tension levels.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: DEPRESSION decreased in male COMP from MID to POST (p < 0.05), though not significantly different from CTRL. No significant changes were observed in female groups.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects feelings of sadness, despondency, and low mood.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Across the MID to POST phase in male and female physique athletes and control groups.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A decrease indicates an improvement in mood and reduction in depressive symptoms during the recovery phase. Stability in females suggests consistent depression levels, indicating different psychological responses compared to males.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decreases were observed among male and female COMP during competition preparation (PRE to MID). Strength returned to baseline after the recovery phase (MID to POST).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the capacity of muscles to exert force; mechanical stimuli from strength training are important for muscle hypertrophy.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During competition preparation and the subsequent recovery phase.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle performance; maintaining muscle strength is an essential goal for preserving fat-free mass and achieving optimal physique outcomes. Decreases during preparation indicate impaired performance, while recovery signifies restoration of muscle function.
